US government adds "advanced robotic devices" to foreign-made product ban list; FCC confirms robot vacuums included

Robot vacuum ban hits Roomba, Roborock and other major brands — but you can keep using your existing unit

When the Trump administration announced a ban on "advanced robotic devices" entering the US yesterday, media attention focused on humanoid robots. Yet espionage doesn't need legs to walk — nor does the FCC's robot ban. Katie Gorscak, the FCC's media relations director, confirmed to The Verge that robot vacuums will also fall within the scope of the ban. Existing Roombas won't be targeted, and companies may continue importing and selling already-approved models. But the government claims future foreign robots will pose national security risks — and even robot vacuum companies have suddenly been asked to commit to manufacturing in the US.

The FCC considers advanced robotic devices a national security risk, and the rule also covers products most people would consider harmless, such as robot vacuums and lawn mowers.

Unless a device is explicitly approved, or made on US soil, it cannot be sold there.

The ban hits the robot vacuum market particularly hard, since major brands including Roomba, Roborock, and Ecovacs are all owned by Chinese companies.

If you already own one, you can keep using it today without issue. The FCC is not sending anyone to confiscate your robot vacuum.

But depending on how the ban is implemented, the robot vacuum market could see sudden upheaval in the short term. If this all sounds familiar, that's because an earlier Wi-Fi router ban played out in much the same way.

Will you continue using your existing robot vacuum, and why? Share your thoughts in the comments.
